### Orchestrator · Question

Event: `bdeb18efc1fc6876a0ed4c9813c6a0ee` · 2026-10-02T21:34:25Z

> From round 1's red BLOCK (F1, R37): an Agent request carried no guard tying its target label set to the caller's, so alice@{7} could submit Agent{[]} and land its audit, lease and agents_started in the unlabelled domain. The implementer has added the labelled half as a Request-table guard (agent_own_set: a labelled caller's Agent names exactly its own set) with its mutation, and P10 now draws [] and foreign sets. The page is silent on the other half: an UNLABELLED caller submitting Agent{[]}. Today it is accepted, audited in its own domain, and on approval starts an unlabelled lease - crossing nothing, but duplicating StartAgent through an approval. Options: (a) allow it and say so on steward.md (a human's approval for a long lease, say); (b) refuse it, an Agent request is for a labelled agent and an unlabelled one is StartAgent, folded into agent_own_set with the page saying so. Your ruling, with a line for the page; the fix round proceeds on the labelled half meanwhile and folds your answer before its report if it arrives in time, else as its last commit.

### Architect · Answer

Event: `b9cbcf6dc32010b1cdf99f79c2014828` · 2026-10-02T21:34:52Z

> Ruled (b): refuse it, folded into agent_own_set.
> 
> Why: an unlabelled caller already starts the same lease with StartAgent, bounded by MAX_LEASE, with no approval. An approved copy of it adds no authority and no check; it is a second way to do one thing (tenet 1). The powerbox is for what a caller lacks: steward.md Leases says "a budget with more labels than its parent needs the steward and an approval". So an Agent request always names a labelled agent.
> 
> The guard: an Agent request names a non-empty label set. A labelled caller's must be exactly its own set (the half already built). An unlabelled caller's may be any set its principal owns; owns_labels already covers that. Agent{[]} is refused from every caller. PolicyAgentOtherSet stays the guard's one mutation, and P10's labelled half catches it. Add a core unit test that pins the unlabelled refusal.
> 
> Page lines. The implementer's branch has already rewritten steward.md (9661299d2), so to avoid a conflict, the implementer folds these in its branch rather than me editing main:
> 
> 1. Leases, at the end of the "Delegation only narrows" bullet: "An agent request asks for a labelled agent: from a labelled session, in exactly its own label set; from an unlabelled session, in a label set its principal owns. An unlabelled agent is started with `StartAgent`, never through an approval."
> 
> 2. Guard table row: | `agent_own_set` | an agent request names a labelled agent: a labelled caller's, exactly its own label set, so its lease and records stay in its domain (R37); an unlabelled agent is `StartAgent`'s | `PolicyAgentOtherSet` |
> 
> I check both at the package's review.
